**Visible observations.** In the close views, the avatar is back-to-camera at the desk; keyboard and mouse sit on the pale mat, while the hands are largely occluded, so key contact is indeterminate. In the wide views, he is seated in the white chair facing the desk/monitor; seat/back contact is occluded. The keyboard is ahead/right of his torso, with the mouse farther right. The nearer hand is on the front desk/mat side of the keyboard, fingers extended, and is not visibly over the key field. The other hand is partly occluded beside its near/left end; finger contact and any 3-D clearance cannot be determined. The definite still-image mismatch is that the visible pose does not show two hands placed on keys. Not established: a measured physical gap, both hands’ contact state, motion, or keystrokes. The privacy message supplies no desktop/typing evidence.

**Acceptance.** Yes—for a typing shot requiring key contact, this blocks acceptance. It does not prove every frame fails, establish input functionality, or diagnose the cause.

**Minimal read-only diagnostic.** At the identical clip phase, using existing inspection facilities, request source identity/hash, original-p5 hand targets/root anchors, source root/pelvis/hand/fingertip FK, reconstructed/retargeted equivalents, and avatar-root/keyboard/desk/chair world transforms. Derive the keyboard key plane and intended key targets; report each fingertip/palm in keyboard coordinates as signed height plus horizontal error, marking occluded values unknown rather than guessing. Offline-read all four manifested sources at the same phase; do not mount or select among them. Matching offsets in original p5 and reconstruction implicate original tuning/source motion; p5 key alignment with reconstruction-only error implicates retarget/root/source-to-scene alignment. Source agreement would not establish asset provenance.
